We've seen a fairy large increase in the number of people submitting their own games and other content to /v/gaming and a few people, including the mods, noticing that these users verge on spamming the 'verse, while not contributing in any other fashion to Voat.

We absolutely don't want to discourage people from sharing their content and helping them out, because there's plenty of quality material being showcased. We want to be supportive of developers/youtubers/writers etc, but there are better ways to go about things! The guidelines below were written by /v/gaming's original mod, and I've taken the time to amend them to bring them up to date. Please try to consider them before posting any of your own content.

  1. Try not to spam the board with your content. Submitting your own Letâ€™s Play or Blog is fine, but if it becomes obviously over the top then we'll look into whether it belongs in /v/gaming.

  2. Do not link to anything that takes payment info. Submit a link to a YouTube video of your game or an article about your game. If you link to to Steam or your own website, try to stick around and respond to users. If you want to sell your game, showcase your game.

  3. Do not artificially UpVoat your posts. Brigading or suspected brigading of content will be deleted. Of course, itâ€™s entirely possible for a moderator to be mistaken please appeal the moderator if you believe there has been a mistake.

  4. Please participate in the board other than just submitting your own content. If you are just coming here to sell us your stuff, it tends to stand out.

Don't forget, Voat's sitewide FAQ is clear on self promotion:

if you submit 10 links to various subverses on Voat, at most 2 of the 10 submitted links may be to the sites you are associated with.

Rule #4 should be highlighted in that, if your an active participant in /v/gaming then we have no issue with you submitting your own content.

These rules mostly apply to those monetised (for obvious reasons); i.e we're not stopping our frequent contributors or going to delete content on a whim.

We ask our users to keep an eye out for these things and let us know!

All of this of course is fully open to feedback and we will always look to the community before giving somebody the cold shoulder. These are guidelines, not rules. Let us know what you think below!

I support these kinds of guidelines. They're a lot more balanced and fair than some of the others I've seen. It takes all different kinds of submissions to make places like this interesting. For a lot of the content we see, if it weren't for the creator posting it, it wouldn't be seen. Not everyone who produces quality content has readership/viewership in the tens/hundreds of thousands where you can count on viewers to link the content for you. If we don't support creators in promoting their content, this place becomes just another outlet for mainstream media.

Conversely, creators have an obligation to be respectful in how (and how often) they post links to their own work. They shouldn't feel like they have open license to post whatever they want whenever they want. Not every blog, vlog, interview or LP episode is a gem.

I personally don't count how many "not mine" submissions I make relative to the ones I make featuring my own content. I'm not about to start. I like the use of the term "guideline". If I haven't posted a link to my own stuff in a few days and then post a link to a short video I made, I don't need to be told about some ratio that I'm not abiding by. If my content isn't relevant to the subverse, obviously it warrants bringing to my attention. If the frequency of my submissions is disruptive, then obviously some poor sod has to bring that to my attention. But if the sole reason for opposing my choice to make the submission is some number relative to some other number based on who is linking whose work then maybe there needs to be a very frank conversation about the risks and consequences of an overly pedantic view on what is or is not appropriate.

And so based on all of that, what I see here seems to have been carefully considered with both "sides" of the equation in mind. Everyone has a role to play, nobody is unjustly excluded, and the community as a whole benefits. Can't complain about that.
